body: (There used to be an AI review comment here that got deleted. This is in response to that.) **D1**: This was indeed an oversight. Fixed. Also rewrote the "a" start tag as a list of steps. **D2**: I don't think this is needed. The speculative HTML parser section already says that "the state of the normal HTML parser and the document itself must not be affected", and that DOM operations are expected to work appropriately on speculative mock elements. **D3**: I added a `video`/`audio` test to web-platform-tests/wpt#64990: a default `metadata` track has to become hidden. I didn't take the `form` render-blocking change, though. Without the ``, the next inline script's `` pops an element, which processes internal resource links before the parser blocks, so the `form` removal stays masked. **Q1**: I'd keep (a). It's not observable today. Only formatting elements reach that step and none of them have children parsed steps. And later in the same adoption agency pass, removing *formattingElement* from the stack processes internal resource links anyway, so `rel=expect` can't tell (a) and (b) apart. Keeping it means every element that leaves the stack runs its children parsed steps.

LGTM
